title: Ask the diver
noMatch: Ooh, I don't know that one yet! Try one of these questions.

items.question: Why is the water brown near Tsawwassen?
items.answer: That's the Fraser River! It brings mud and fresh water down from the mountains. Right now the sea here has {salinity} grams of salt in every litre. The open ocean has about 35!
items.fallback: That's the Fraser River! It brings mud and fresh water down from the mountains, so the sea near Tsawwassen is much less salty than the open ocean.

items.question: How deep is it here?
items.answer: Right under us the sea is about {depth} metres deep. That's about {houses} houses stacked on top of each other!
items.fallback: In the middle of the Strait the sea is more than 200 metres deep. That's taller than a 60-storey tower!

items.question: What's a tide?
items.answer: Twice a day the Moon pulls the sea up a little and then lets it drop again. Here the water goes up and down by about 3 metres. That's taller than a grown-up!

items.question: Why does the ferry wiggle in Active Pass?
items.answer: Active Pass is narrow and twisty, with strong currents. The ferry turns hard and the water swirls, so we rock a little. Hold on!

items.question: What do the sensors on this ship measure?
items.answer: Ocean Networks Canada sensors under the ferry check the sea every second: how warm it is, how salty, how much oxygen, how many tiny plants and how cloudy. Right now the water is {waterTemp} °C!
items.fallback: Ocean Networks Canada sensors under the ferry check the sea every second: how warm it is, how salty, how much oxygen, how many tiny plants and how cloudy.

items.question: What lives under the ferry?
items.answer: Salmon, orcas, seals, jellyfish, crabs and big forests of kelp! And deep down there are glass sponge reefs older than the pyramids.
